ui.subTitle1: Establish a scientific safety management system
ui.subTitle2: based on HSE guidelines and Quantitative Risk Assessment.

def.generalContent: Tasks performed frequently where hazards are effectively mitigated through established Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
def.highContent: Activities involving hazardous energy or complex environments where a single failure can result in a fatality or catastrophic incident.

tasks.c: Work in any place where, if precautions were not taken, a person could fall a distance liable to cause personal injury.
Entry into areas with limited access and potential for toxic atmosphere or O2 deficiency.
Welding, cutting, or brazing activities that produce sparks or open flames.
Rigging and hoisting loads using cranes, derricks, or powered industrial equipment (LOLER).
Work on energised equipment or within limited approach boundaries (Electricity at Work Regs).
Ground disturbance where cave-ins or underground utility strikes are potential hazards.
Industrial radiography or NDT tasks involving exposure to radiation sources (IRR17).
Transfer, charging, or processing of toxic, flammable, or reactive hazardous substances (COSHH).
Lockout/Tagout procedures during maintenance to control hazardous energy.
